Action: obtain the compliance calculation or the credit agreement definitions. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21 - High: reported EBITDA for fiscal 2024 is negative, so total debt and net debt over reported EBITDA are not calculable for that year and are shown as not supplied in the leverage table. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 99 - Medium: fiscal 2025 has 53 weeks with a 14-week fourth quarter, so every twelve-month figure to October 3, 2026 spans 53 weeks. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation R3 - Medium: the twelve-month adjusted EBITDA mixes two add-back definitions by about USD 1,134 thousand, or 0.40%, because losses on sales and disposals of property, plant and equipment are added back from 2026 but not in the fiscal 2025 report. Action: obtain the issuer's restated fiscal 2025 adjusted EBITDA. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-Q_2026-04-04_bgs_bgs-20260404x10q.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation R14 - Medium: the balance sheet at July 4, 2026 carries both the 2027 and the 2031 notes and cash of USD 591,576 thousand because the redemption was paid on July 6, 2026; gross debt and cash for that date are not comparable. Action: read the July 4, 2026 liquidity and net debt rows with the redemption timing. Action: confirm against the next quarterly report. The $475.0 million of 11.00% notes due 2031 replaced $509.3 million of 5.25% notes due 2027, which lifts the annual coupon on those principal amounts by $25.51 million. The new notes raised $463.9 million at their issue price, $45.4 million less than the redemption amount, so cash and the revolver covered the gap, and net revolver borrowings were $140.0 million over the first three quarters of 2026. facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the underlying business has stopped shrinking and is earning more on what is left. Base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 on volume growth of 1.4%, adjusted gross profit was 22.3% of net sales against 21.6% a year earlier as higher-margin broth brands joined, a lower-margin frozen business left and tariff expense fell, and the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at the latest quarter end. The 2031 notes also remove the 2027 maturity, so no bond matures before September 2028, and the halved dividend keeps roughly $29.8 million a year inside the business. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Since May 2025 the issuer has sold four brand groups and bought one. The Don Pepino and Sclafani brands (May 23, 2025, $10.6 million), the Le Sueur brand in the United States (August 1, 2025, $59.1 million), the Green Giant frozen business in the United States (March 2, 2026, about $61.5 million, with a continuing co-manufacturing agreement) and the B&M and Joan of Arc brands (October 13, 2026, $8.0 million, after the quarter end) were sold. The College Inn and Kitchen Basics broth brands were bought on March 19, 2026 for $109.7 million in cash, after an agreement dated January 15, 2026. The issuer says the purpose is to sharpen focus, improve margins and reduce long-term debt. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On June 10, 2026 the issuer sold $475.0 million of 11.00% senior notes due 2031 at 97.67% of face value. The notes are unsecured, are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries, pay interest each June 15 and December 15 from December 15, 2026, and can be called at 105.50% from June 15, 2028. With revolver borrowings and cash, the proceeds redeemed all $509.3 million of the 5.25% senior notes due 2027 at par, with the redemption date July 4, 2026 and payment on July 6, 2026, after the second-quarter balance-sheet date, and a $1.1 million loss on extinguishment. Debt financing costs paid in the first three quarters of 2026 were $18.4 million against $0.9 million a year earlier, and the issuer borrowed $180.0 million and repaid $40.0 million under the revolver. The 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 ($799.3 million outstanding) rank equally with the credit agreement and ahead of the new unsecured notes to the extent of the collateral. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Earlier debt actions set the structure. The issuer sold $550.0 million of the 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 on September 26, 2023 at 99.502% of face value and a further $250.0 million on July 12, 2024 at 100.5%, when it also cut the term loans from $507.3 million to $450.0 million with maturity extended to October 2029 and cut revolver capacity from $800.0 million to $475.0 million, and redeemed the $265.4 million of 5.25% notes due 2025 on October 9, 2024 with revolver loans and cash. On July 1, 2025 the credit agreement was amended to cut revolver commitments from $475.0 million to $430.0 million and to raise the maximum leverage ratio temporarily, for a $0.8 million fee. During 2025 the issuer also bought $20.7 million (second quarter) and $20.0 million (third quarter) of the 2027 notes in the open market at 89.98% and 96.00% of face value. The supplied filings state at-the-market equity sales of $66.6 million gross in fiscal 2022 and $75.3 million gross in fiscal 2023, with the net proceeds used to repay, redeem or repurchase long-term debt, pay offering costs and for general corporate purposes, and none in fiscal 2024; the cash flow statements show no stock issuance proceeds in fiscal 2025 or the first three quarters of 2026. facts.label: T2D.9 — Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by distributions that exceeded operating cash flow before the 2026 cut, debt that rose while the portfolio was reshaped and a leadership transition under way, because they weaken liquidity and add execution risk, which implies more reliance on refinancing access. Countervailing evidence is the halved dividend, the extended maturity, regular and audited reporting, compliance with covenants and the absence of any creditor-adverse transaction in the supplied filings. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the report on Form 8-K filed August 11, 2026.

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: The issuer is a listed holding company whose domestic subsidiaries guarantee its debt, while foreign subsidiaries do not guarantee the 2031 notes. Ownership is dispersed and no sponsor or controlling holder is identified in the supplied filings, although the proxy statement that would show large holders was not supplied. The board sets financial policy: the stated policy distributes a substantial portion of available cash, the dividend rate was halved in 2026 and the board can change it at any time. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Net sales fell 6.30% in fiscal 2024 and 5.37% in fiscal 2025, which the issuer states as 5.4% and attributes mainly to lower base business sales, and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, mostly through divestitures. Base business net sales fell 4.0% in fiscal 2025 on volume down 3.5% and price and mix down 0.3%, and rose 1.8% in 2026 on volume up 1.4% and price and mix up 0.3%. Pricing power is limited: the issuer says price increases may lag costs and competition can limit quick increases, retailers push for lower prices and more promotion and favour private label, and part of the Spices & Flavor Solutions growth came from private label and foodservice. Revenue is therefore predictable as staple demand but structurally pressured by channel shifts and concentrated in one buyer, so creditors can lean on the 2026 volume turn only if it persists for several quarters. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Gross profit was 21.8% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and 21.4% in the first three quarters of 2026, so small cost movements matter, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 15.88% of net sales over the twelve months against 14.88% in fiscal 2025 and 15.29% in fiscal 2024. Inputs are agricultural products, oils, packaging and freight; the issuer is locked into supply and prices for most key raw materials only through the end of fiscal 2026 and expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. The largest segment shows the pressure: Specialty adjusted EBITDA fell 19.4% over nine months on higher oil input costs for Crisco and diesel-driven logistics costs, while Spices & Flavor Solutions rose 21.9% on pricing, lower spice costs and lower tariff expense that includes refunds; the Don Pepino sale also played a small part in the Specialty fall. Margins can be defended only where pricing catches up with costs, and part of the group improvement is one-off, so margin stability is average at best. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital expenditure is low, $30.6 million in fiscal 2025 and $17.8 million in the first three quarters of 2026, with $25.0 million or less planned for fiscal 2026, and the business is seasonal, buying produce from June to October and maple syrup from April to August. Twelve-month free cash flow was 34.96% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA, but a large rise in trade payables lifted operating cash flow and can reverse, and acquisition, divestiture-related and non-recurring costs recur while the portfolio is reshaped: the amount added back to issuer-adjusted EBITDA was $32,427 thousand in the first three quarters of 2026 against $9,993 thousand a year earlier, which is largely cash leaving the business. Cash interest is the largest fixed claim and is rising, because the 2031 notes replaced lower-cost notes and the first coupon on them falls due on December 15, 2026. Cash conversion is adequate before dividends and weak after them, which is why the dividend cut matters to creditors. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense: the issuer competes with numerous companies, including larger and less leveraged ones, and with private label, so margin depends on brand strength in each category. Buyer power is the strongest force, with one retailer at 31.0% of net sales, ten customers at 63.6% and consolidating retailers demanding lower prices and more promotion. Supplier power is moderate: inputs are commodities bought under short contracts or advance purchases, Green Giant vegetables come under dedicated acreage contracts and a significant part of production is outsourced to co-packers who serve other companies. The threat of substitutes comes from private label and alternative outlets such as warehouse clubs, dollar stores and e-commerce, and the threat of new entrants is not quantified in the supplied filings. For creditors the forces cap pricing power and make volume the main lever for earnings. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Trade policy and fuel costs are the factors that alter credit quality. Tariffs on imported spices and steel cans raised costs, tariff refunds followed a February 2026 court ruling and some may have to be shared with customers, and retaliation could hurt sales in Canada. Diesel and freight costs rose in 2026 and the issuer expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the supplied materials, apart from the shift toward e-commerce and private label already counted under competition. For creditors the tariff refund is a non-recurring gain to earnings and fuel costs are a recurring margin risk. facts.label: Credit-translated SWOT
facts.text: Strengths are established brands with stabilising volumes, low capital intensity, a halved dividend and no bond maturity before September 2028. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are average: net sales of $1,791.549 million over twelve months are falling, through lower base sales in fiscal 2025 and disposals in 2026, and the issuer's category leadership claims cannot be benchmarked because no peer data was supplied. Competitive advantage is average, resting on brands the issuer calls leaders in their categories but under retailer and private-label pressure. Business diversification is average, with four segments but one dominant customer. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and the dividend has been cut, but the split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed and the issuer has not yet priced through input costs. Margin stability is weak to average, with the largest segment's earnings falling and group gains partly one-off. Free cash flow stability is weak, since cash flow falls short of dividends in the first three quarters of both 2025 and 2026 and rising interest absorbs more. The ability to refinance is average to weak, with market access shown at a high cost and $1,157.69 million due in fiscal 2028. Liquidity is weak, with $116.84 million of cash and availability at October 3, 2026, the seasonal peak. Financial policy and governance are average, with a creditor-friendlier dividend but a leadership change and no identified owner. The trend is stabilising operations against deteriorating liquidity and coverage, and the key missing data points are the covenant calculation and the credit agreement definitions. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are base business volume growth, a dividend cost of $30.8 million a year in fiscal 2027, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, supply and prices locked for most key materials through the end of fiscal 2026 and a possible sale of the Green Giant Canada business. The headwinds are the first full year of the 2031 notes, with the first coupon due on December 15, 2026, freight elevated into fiscal 2027, labour agreements at two Specialty plants expiring on March 30 and April 30, 2027, covenant step-downs on January 2 and April 3, 2027 and the leadership transition. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing the 2028 maturities with covenants tighter and a portfolio smaller than today. The supplied filings give no guidance for sales or earnings, so these items are directional and carry no forecast. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario replays the issuer's own fiscal 2025 experience. The initiating condition is a retailer or category setback that cuts net sales by 5.37%, the fall seen in fiscal 2025, from the twelve-month level of $1,791.549 million. The first operational break is lost volume with costs for oil, fuel and freight still rising, and in fiscal 2025 each dollar of lost net sales coincided with 22.37 cents of lost issuer-adjusted EBITDA. On that ratio net sales fall $96.20 million and issuer-adjusted EBITDA falls $21.52 million to $263.04 million, which takes net debt to 7.52x issuer-adjusted EBITDA from 6.95x and cover on run-rate interest to 1.55x from 1.68x. Free cash flow falls by about the lost earnings before tax while cash interest steps up to its run-rate of $169.74 million, so the seasonal build would rely on $55.1 million of revolver availability. Management levers are the remaining dividend of $30.8 million a year, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, inventory release and a sale of the Canadian business. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months, because no bond matures before September 2028, but the covenant step-downs to 7.25x and 7.00x would be the first break and cannot be tested here, and a covenant breach would put the 2028 refinancing at risk. The observable triggers are base business net sales, Specialty adjusted EBITDA, revolver availability and the compliance statements in each quarterly report. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months, because no bond matures before September 2028, but the covenant step-downs to 7.25x and 7.00x would be the first break and cannot be tested here, and a covenant breach would put the 2028 refinancing at risk. The observable triggers are base business net sales, Specialty adjusted EBITDA, revolver availability and the compliance statements in each quarterly report.

# CP-1 Financial foundation: B&G Foods, Inc.
## Request

B&G Foods, Inc. (issuer bgs-1278027), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the financial foundation: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage from the five supplied filings, with the source readiness answer as context.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt is 6.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA but 15.00x reported EBITDA on twelve-month figures at the latest quarter, so creditors hold a heavily geared balance sheet and the lower ratio depends on large add-backs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; calculation R4; calculation R5; calculation R9

Cover is thin: issuer-adjusted EBITDA is 2.08x cash interest and reported EBITDA is only 0.96x, before the full-year cost of the 11.00% notes that replaced the 5.25% notes. Undrawn revolver capacity net of letters of credit has fallen to USD 55.1 million from USD 207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025, and borrowings and asset sales, not operating cash, funded the 2026 acquisition and dividends. Debt maturities are concentrated in 2028, and the twelve-month figures span 53 weeks.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation R6; calculation R10; calculation R18
### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Net debt rose by USD 84,328 thousand in the 39 weeks to October 3, 2026, to USD 1,978,111 thousand, because the USD 109,655 thousand acquisition of the College Inn and Kitchen Basics brands and USD 38,341 thousand of dividends outran USD 61,437 thousand of asset sale proceeds and USD 29,566 thousand of operating cash flow. The consequence is that deleveraging now depends on further disposals and cost savings rather than on cash generation. The revolver's maximum leverage ratio steps down from 7.50x to 7.25x for the quarter ending January 2, 2027 and to 7.00x from April 3, 2027, but headroom is not established because the covenant's own EBITDA and net debt definitions are not reproduced in the filings.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation R1; calculation R2

Gross leverage on reported EBITDA is 11.60x for fiscal 2025 and 15.46x for the twelve months to October 3, 2026, but reported EBITDA is depressed by non-cash impairments and by the loss on the Green Giant frozen sale, which the issuer adds back; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA the same ratios are 7.16x and 7.17x. The strongest contrary reading is that the add-backs are largely non-cash, which would make the adjusted ratio the better guide to debt service; against that, impairments in fiscal 2024, fiscal 2025 and again in the third quarter of 2026, with reported EBITDA negative in fiscal 2024, show an asset base losing value, so the adjusted ratio may understate the risk that brand values cannot support the debt in a sale or restructuring.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation R4; calculation R5; calculation R9
### Coverage and interest burden

Cash interest paid was USD 149,039 thousand in fiscal 2025 and USD 137,053 thousand over the twelve months to October 3, 2026. The cost of debt is rising because the 11.00% notes due 2031 replaced the 5.25% notes due 2027, so cover of 2.08x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA is more likely to fall than rise unless EBITDA grows, and on reported EBITDA it is already below 1.00x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation R6; calculation R10
### Cash-flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 29,566 thousand for the 39 weeks of 2026 against USD 5,950 thousand a year earlier, helped by a USD 58,481 thousand rise in trade payables that reverses if suppliers are paid faster, while inventories absorbed USD 75,445 thousand. After capital expenditures of USD 17,752 thousand, free cash flow was USD 11,814 thousand, well below the USD 38,341 thousand of dividends paid; the issuer has since halved its dividend rate and drew on the revolver to fund the shortfall, which is a direct claim on liquidity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation R11; calculation R12
### Liquidity adequacy

Cash of USD 61,743 thousand plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 55.1 million, net of USD 19.9 million of letters of credit, is the whole stated liquidity buffer, and undrawn capacity has fallen at every quarter end of 2026. The 8.00% senior secured notes mature on September 15, 2028 and the revolver on December 16, 2028, so about USD 1,157.69 million falls due in fiscal 2028, which is the main refinancing pressure point; nothing but term loan amortization matures in the next twelve months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation R13; calculation R18
### Data-quality and definition risks

The period basis is not clean: fiscal 2025 has 53 weeks with a 14-week fourth quarter, so the twelve-month figures to October 3, 2026 span 53 weeks. From the first quarter of 2026 the issuer also adds back losses on sales and disposals of property, plant and equipment, which the fiscal 2025 annual report did not, so the twelve-month adjusted EBITDA mixes two definitions by about USD 1,134 thousand, or 0.40%. This does not change the leverage conclusion, but covenant tests are defined on the credit agreement's own EBITDA, which the filings do not reproduce, so covenant headroom is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 50–52; 10-Q_2026-04-04_bgs_bgs-20260404x10q.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation R3; calculation R14

The July 4, 2026 balance sheet shows total debt of USD 2,522,281 thousand and cash of USD 591,576 thousand because the 2031 notes were issued on June 10, 2026 and the 2027 notes were redeemed only on July 6, 2026; net debt there is largely unaffected, but gross debt and cash both are, so the second quarter position is kept out of the ratios. After the October 3, 2026 balance sheet the issuer sold the B&M and Joan of Arc brands and paid a dividend, and the agreement to sell Green Giant Canada was terminated on October 5, 2026; none of these is in the period figures.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors should treat B&G Foods as a shrinking-sales, customer-concentrated branded-food credit that is reshaping its portfolio and has accepted a much higher coupon to move its nearest bond maturity to September 2028, with no identified sponsor to support or drain it.

The portfolio changes since 2025 trade a lower-margin frozen business and small shelf-stable brands for higher-margin broth brands, and the board halved the dividend rate, which reduces cash leakage. The open questions are who leads the company after the chief executive's retirement in August 2026 and who holds the shares, because the successor and the proxy statement are not in the supplied documents.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-Q_2026-07-04_bgs_bgs-20260704x10q.htm.jsonl, page 36; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- Customer concentration is the operating fact that matters most for cash-flow stability: one retailer, Walmart, took 31.0% of fiscal 2025 net sales and the ten largest customers took 63.6%, so one negotiation on price, promotions or shelf space can move a large part of earnings. The retailer's share eased to 28.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, and it held about the same share of trade receivables at the quarter end.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that the underlying business has stopped shrinking and is earning more on what is left. Base business net sales rose 1.8% in the first three quarters of 2026 on volume growth of 1.4%, adjusted gross profit was 22.3% of net sales against 21.6% a year earlier as higher-margin broth brands joined, a lower-margin frozen business left and tariff expense fell, and the issuer reports compliance with every covenant at the latest quarter end. The 2031 notes also remove the 2027 maturity, so no bond matures before September 2028, and the halved dividend keeps roughly $29.8 million a year inside the business.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation A8

Three developments would turn the view more constructive: a named chief executive with a stated plan for the disposal programme, a completed sale of the Green Giant Canada business with proceeds applied to the revolver, and a proxy statement showing a large holder committed to the equity. Three would turn it more negative: base business net sales falling again, a further failed or discounted disposal, and a change in terms from the largest customer. A covenant ratio close to its limit would also change the view, but the supplied filings do not print the ratios.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Since May 2025 the issuer has sold four brand groups and bought one. The Don Pepino and Sclafani brands (May 23, 2025, $10.6 million), the Le Sueur brand in the United States (August 1, 2025, $59.1 million), the Green Giant frozen business in the United States (March 2, 2026, about $61.5 million, with a continuing co-manufacturing agreement) and the B&M and Joan of Arc brands (October 13, 2026, $8.0 million, after the quarter end) were sold. The College Inn and Kitchen Basics broth brands were bought on March 19, 2026 for $109.7 million in cash, after an agreement dated January 15, 2026. The issuer says the purpose is to sharpen focus, improve margins and reduce long-term debt.

A sale of the Green Giant business in Canada to Nortera Foods, agreed on October 24, 2025 at inventory value plus $5.0 million (about $60.0 million on September 27, 2025 inventory), was terminated by mutual agreement on October 5, 2026 because Canadian competition approval had not been obtained by September 24, 2026. The issuer still classifies the assets as held for sale ($52.9 million at October 3, 2026), says it continues to pursue a sale and believes one is probable within a year; no buyer or price is stated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 39

On June 10, 2026 the issuer sold $475.0 million of 11.00% senior notes due 2031 at 97.67% of face value. The notes are unsecured, are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries, pay interest each June 15 and December 15 from December 15, 2026, and can be called at 105.50% from June 15, 2028. With revolver borrowings and cash, the proceeds redeemed all $509.3 million of the 5.25% senior notes due 2027 at par, with the redemption date July 4, 2026 and payment on July 6, 2026, after the second-quarter balance-sheet date, and a $1.1 million loss on extinguishment. Debt financing costs paid in the first three quarters of 2026 were $18.4 million against $0.9 million a year earlier, and the issuer borrowed $180.0 million and repaid $40.0 million under the revolver. The 8.00% senior secured notes due 2028 ($799.3 million outstanding) rank equally with the credit agreement and ahead of the new unsecured notes to the extent of the collateral.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors should treat B&G Foods as a highly leveraged, thinly covered branded-food credit whose steady base business can service debt to 2028 only if liquidity is not drawn down further and the 2028 maturities are refinanced; refinancing, not operations, decides the outcome.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 21; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is near seven times issuer-adjusted EBITDA and about fifteen times reported EBITDA, cash interest cover is about two times, and revolver availability has fallen to $55.1 million. The base business is growing again and the dividend is halved, but the largest segment's earnings are falling and covenant headroom cannot be shown.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation K1; calculation K3
### Key findings

- Leverage and cover are the binding weakness. Net debt is 6.95x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and 15.00x reported EBITDA at the latest quarter end, and twelve-month issuer-adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest paid 2.08x, with reported EBITDA at 0.96x. Pro forma for the October 13, 2026 sale of the B&M and Joan of Arc brands, net leverage on reported EBITDA is 14.93x, and 15.05x after the October 30, 2026 dividend; the issuer-adjusted pro forma is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K3

- The interest burden is rising after the June 2026 refinancing. At October 3, 2026 balances and printed rates, contractual cash interest is $169.74 million a year, $32.69 million more than the cash interest paid over the twelve months, which takes cover on issuer-adjusted EBITDA to 1.68x. The credit agreement sets a minimum interest cover of 1.75x on its own definitions, which the filings do not reproduce, so headroom is not established, but the two measures are close enough that the definitions are the first document to obtain.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-10-03_bgs_bgs-20261003x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2026-01-03_bgs_bgs-20260103x10k.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation K4; calculation K5

- Liquidity is thin and shrinking at the seasonal peak. Revolver availability fell from $207.6 million at the end of fiscal 2025 to $55.1 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026, and cash plus availability totals $116.84 million at that date, with the pro forma effect on cash of the October 13, 2026 brand sale and the October 30, 2026 dividend not established, while the issuer says its liquidity needs are greatest from June to October. No bond matures before September 2028, so the risk is a squeeze on liquidity rather than a near-term maturity.

### Credit-relevant company description

B&G Foods sells branded shelf-stable and frozen food and household products, mostly in the United States, through four segments, and its cash flow rests on long-established brands in categories the issuer itself describes as often flat to modestly declining. The portfolio is being reshaped: four brand sales since May 2025 and one acquisition have lowered reported net sales while the issuer says they raise margin. Revenue visibility is moderate because the products are staples bought through large retailers, but concentration is high, with one customer at 31.0% of net sales and contract terms not disclosed. For creditors the business supports steady, low-growth cash flow that can service debt only while costs and retailer terms stay stable.

The issuer is a listed holding company whose domestic subsidiaries guarantee its debt, while foreign subsidiaries do not guarantee the 2031 notes. Net sales fell 6.30% in fiscal 2024 and 5.37% in fiscal 2025, which the issuer states as 5.4% and attributes mainly to lower base business sales, and 2.9% in the first three quarters of 2026, mostly through divestitures. Base business net sales fell 4.0% in fiscal 2025 on volume down 3.5% and price and mix down 0.3%, and rose 1.8% in 2026 on volume up 1.4% and price and mix up 0.3%. Pricing power is limited: the issuer says price increases may lag costs and competition can limit quick increases, retailers push for lower prices and more promotion and favour private label, and part of the Spices & Flavor Solutions growth came from private label and foodservice. ### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense: the issuer competes with numerous companies, including larger and less leveraged ones, and with private label, so margin depends on brand strength in each category. Buyer power is the strongest force, with one retailer at 31.0% of net sales, ten customers at 63.6% and consolidating retailers demanding lower prices and more promotion. Supplier power is moderate: inputs are commodities bought under short contracts or advance purchases, Green Giant vegetables come under dedicated acreage contracts and a significant part of production is outsourced to co-packers who serve other companies. The threat of substitutes comes from private label and alternative outlets such as warehouse clubs, dollar stores and e-commerce, and the threat of new entrants is not quantified in the supplied filings. For creditors the forces cap pricing power and make volume the main lever for earnings.

### Macro and policy factors

Trade policy and fuel costs are the factors that alter credit quality. Tariffs on imported spices and steel cans raised costs, tariff refunds followed a February 2026 court ruling and some may have to be shared with customers, and retaliation could hurt sales in Canada. Diesel and freight costs rose in 2026 and the issuer expects freight to stay elevated into fiscal 2027. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the supplied materials, apart from the shift toward e-commerce and private label already counted under competition. For creditors the tariff refund is a non-recurring gain to earnings and fuel costs are a recurring margin risk.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are established brands with stabilising volumes, low capital intensity, a halved dividend and no bond maturity before September 2028. Weaknesses are leverage near seven times issuer-adjusted EBITDA, thin cover, a shrinking revolver cushion, one customer at 31.0% of net sales and a largest segment whose earnings are falling. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are a completed sale of the Green Giant Canada business with proceeds applied to the revolver, continued base business volume growth and pricing that catches up with costs. Threats that could weaken it are cost inflation in oil and fuel, retailer demands for price and promotion, tariff changes and the covenant step-downs in 2027.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: net sales of $1,791.549 million over twelve months are falling, through lower base sales in fiscal 2025 and disposals in 2026, and the issuer's category leadership claims cannot be benchmarked because no peer data was supplied. Competitive advantage is average, resting on brands the issuer calls leaders in their categories but under retailer and private-label pressure. Business diversification is average, with four segments but one dominant customer. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low and the dividend has been cut, but the split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed and the issuer has not yet priced through input costs. Margin stability is weak to average, with the largest segment's earnings falling and group gains partly one-off. Free cash flow stability is weak, since cash flow falls short of dividends in the first three quarters of both 2025 and 2026 and rising interest absorbs more. The ability to refinance is average to weak, with market access shown at a high cost and $1,157.69 million due in fiscal 2028. Liquidity is weak, with $116.84 million of cash and availability at October 3, 2026, the seasonal peak. Financial policy and governance are average, with a creditor-friendlier dividend but a leadership change and no identified owner. The trend is stabilising operations against deteriorating liquidity and coverage, and the key missing data points are the covenant calculation and the credit agreement definitions.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are base business volume growth, a dividend cost of $30.8 million a year in fiscal 2027, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, supply and prices locked for most key materials through the end of fiscal 2026 and a possible sale of the Green Giant Canada business. The headwinds are the first full year of the 2031 notes, with the first coupon due on December 15, 2026, freight elevated into fiscal 2027, labour agreements at two Specialty plants expiring on March 30 and April 30, 2027, covenant step-downs on January 2 and April 3, 2027 and the leadership transition. Over three to five years the issue is refinancing the 2028 maturities with covenants tighter and a portfolio smaller than today. The supplied filings give no guidance for sales or earnings, so these items are directional and carry no forecast.

### Downside scenario

The scenario replays the issuer's own fiscal 2025 experience. The initiating condition is a retailer or category setback that cuts net sales by 5.37%, the fall seen in fiscal 2025, from the twelve-month level of $1,791.549 million. The first operational break is lost volume with costs for oil, fuel and freight still rising, and in fiscal 2025 each dollar of lost net sales coincided with 22.37 cents of lost issuer-adjusted EBITDA. On that ratio net sales fall $96.20 million and issuer-adjusted EBITDA falls $21.52 million to $263.04 million, which takes net debt to 7.52x issuer-adjusted EBITDA from 6.95x and cover on run-rate interest to 1.55x from 1.68x. Free cash flow falls by about the lost earnings before tax while cash interest steps up to its run-rate of $169.74 million, so the seasonal build would rely on $55.1 million of revolver availability. Management levers are the remaining dividend of $30.8 million a year, capital expenditure of $25.0 million or less, inventory release and a sale of the Canadian business. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months, because no bond matures before September 2028, but the covenant step-downs to 7.25x and 7.00x would be the first break and cannot be tested here, and a covenant breach would put the 2028 refinancing at risk. The observable triggers are base business net sales, Specialty adjusted EBITDA, revolver availability and the compliance statements in each quarterly report.

### Overall credit view

Overall, B&G Foods presents an adequate business profile supported by established brands with stabilising volumes, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover and a narrow revolver cushion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate before dividends and weak after them, because capital expenditure is low but cash interest is rising and cash flow has fallen short of dividends. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on base business growth, the largest segment's margin recovering, liquidity being rebuilt and covenant room being shown before the 2028 maturities become current. The primary downside path is renewed sales and margin pressure in the largest segment feeding a covenant step-down in 2027 and a harder 2028 refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreement definitions and compliance calculations, the proxy statement and any guidance. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 maturities after covenant step-downs.
